    AI Overview
    Belve is a popular Italian television interview show hosted by journalist Francesca Fagnani, known for its sharp, direct questions and high-profile guests, airing on Rai 2 and streaming on RaiPlay. Since its 2018 debut, it has gained significant popularity—particularly on social media—and moved to prime time, featuring interviews with celebrities and public figures. 
    Key details about Belve include: 
    • Host & Creator: Created and hosted by Francesca Fagnani, along with Irene Ghergo.
    • Format: A conversational program where the host asks deep, often intense questions of guests, including actors, politicians, and media personalities.
    • Growth: Originally aired on Nove (2018–2019) before moving to Rai 2 in 2021, gaining huge traction on platforms like TikTok and Instagram
      .
    • Availability: Episodes can be watched on RaiPlay, and in 2026, it was announced as part of a deal to appear on Disney+. 
    Note: There is also a hip-hop artist named BELVE based in Detroit and a Filipino beauty brand.

    What is the meaning of belve?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    "Belve" is the plural form of the Italian word bestia or belva, translating to "wild animals," "beasts," or "savages" in English. It is commonly used to describe fierce beasts, as well as a popular Italian television interview show hosted by Francesca Fagnani. Other contexts include an old English regional term for shouting (belving) or a misinterpretation of "belyve" (quickly). 
    Usage Examples & Contexts 
    • Italian Translation (Wild Animals/Beasts): It frequently refers to wild animals or fierce, predatory creatures. Examples include: le belve feroci (ferocious beasts).
    • Metaphorical (Savages): In Italian, belve can be used to describe cruel or savage human beings
      .
    • Belve (TV Series): It is the title of a well-known Italian TV show featuring intense interviews, often highlighting tough, "predatory" questioning of guests. 
    Synonyms & Related Terms 
    • Bestie (Italian): Beasts.
    • Animali selvaggi (Italian): Wild animals.
    • Belva (Italian, Singular): Beast.
    • Belving (English regional): Shouting, roaring, or bellowing, often used to describe hounds. 
    Note: In some contexts, this is confused with the Scots adverb belyve, which means "speedily," "quickly," or "by and by".
